_README: PLACEHOLDER — NOT THE AUTHORITATIVE DEFINITION OF THIS COHORT.
The real logic lives in inst/sql/sql_server/9100001.sql, which is
hand-authored and must never be regenerated from this file.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL: CohortGenerator::getCohortDefinitionSet()
requires a JSON to exist for every row in Cohorts.csv, and Strategus'
createCohortSharedResourceSpecifications() stores its contents in the
analysis specification. So the file must be present and parseable.
WHY IT CANNOT BE THE REAL DEFINITION: non-home discharge is decided by
visit_occurrence.discharged_to_concept_id, and circe 1.11.3 (the version
inside CirceR 1.3.3) has no such attribute. Verified 2026-08-02 by
inspecting org.ohdsi.circe.cohortdefinition.VisitOccurrence, whose full
attribute set is: CodesetId, First, OccurrenceStartDate, OccurrenceEndDate,
VisitType(+Exclude), VisitSourceConcept, VisitLength, Gender,
ProviderSpecialty, PlaceOfService, PlaceOfServiceLocation. VisitDetail is
the same. Circe also cannot express the dynamic UB04 'Maps to' CTE or the
discharged_to_source_value tab/CR/LF normalisation the real SQL performs.
THE DANGER THIS FILE POSES: the expression below entered as ALL inpatient
visits. If anyone ever runs CirceR::buildCohortQuery() over this file and
writes the result to 9100001.sql, the NHD cohort silently becomes 'every
inpatient admission' — an enormous outcome rate that still produces
plausible-looking metrics. CreateStrategusAnalysisSpecification.R carries a
sentinel guard that stops the build if 9100001.sql loses its UB04 CTE.
